steps.say: A taxi charges £3 just to get in, then £2 for every mile. No algebra, just work out the fares.

steps.hint: £3 to start, then £2 for each of the 4 miles: 3 + 2 × 4.

steps.say: Without noticing, you did the £2 × 4 first and added the £3 after. Multiplying before adding is BIDMAS.

steps.hint: £3 plus £2 for each of the 6 miles.

steps.say: That rule, fare = 3 + 2 × miles, is a formula. Writing miles as a letter gives \(f = 3 + 2m\). Putting a number in place of \(m\) and working it out is substitution, and it is the whole of this lesson.

steps: Replace each letter with its value, using brackets around negatives.
Follow BIDMAS: powers, then multiply or divide, then add or subtract.
To change the subject, undo operations in reverse with the inverse of each.
method_card.title: Substitute and Rearrange Formulae
method_card.content:
Substitution swaps letters for given numbers, then evaluates with BIDMAS. Brackets around a negative keep its sign safe, so \((-3)^2 = 9\).

Rearranging (changing the subject) isolates one letter using inverse operations in reverse BIDMAS order. Whatever you do to one side, do to the other, then test with a number.

steps: Rearranging means getting one letter on its own using inverse operations.
Work in reverse BIDMAS: undo adding and subtracting first, then multiplying and dividing, then powers with a root.
Whatever you do to one side, do to the other. A quick number test proves the result.
gold.title: Gold: changing the subject

steps: Substitute means swap each letter for the number you are given, then work out the result.
Follow BIDMAS: do any multiplication or division before addition or subtraction.
Write the calculation out fully before you touch the arithmetic. It stops silly slips.
bronze.title: Bronze: substituting single values

steps: Deal with powers first: square the value before any multiply or add.
Put negative values in brackets so the sign is safe: \((-3)^2 = 9\), not \(-9\).
Then finish with BIDMAS: multiplications, then additions and subtractions.
silver.title: Silver: powers and negative values

gold.hint: Subtract 2 from both sides, then divide by 5.

misconceptions.message: To undo +2 you subtract, not add. Subtract 2 from both sides to get y − 2 = 5x, then divide by 5. Adding gives (y + 2)/5, which is wrong.
Undo the +2 before the ×5. Subtract 2 first, then divide the whole side by 5. Dividing first gives y/5 − 2, which is wrong.

gold.hint: Subtract u from both sides, then divide by a.
gold.display: Make \(t\) the subject of \(v = u + at\)

misconceptions.message: To undo +u you subtract it: v − u = at, then divide by a. Adding u gives (v + u)/a, which is wrong.

misconceptions.note: subtract a instead of divide -> option 2
misconceptions.message: a multiplies t, so undo it by dividing, not subtracting. After v − u = at, divide by a. Subtracting a gives v − u − a, which is wrong.

gold.hint: Divide by pi first, then take the square root.

misconceptions.message: Dividing by π gives r² = A/π, but you must still undo the square by taking a root. Stopping at A/π forgets that step.
Divide by π before rooting. r² = A/π, so r = √(A/π). Rooting only the A, giving √A/π, undoes things in the wrong order.

gold.hint: Multiply both sides by 2, then divide by h.

misconceptions.message: The half must be undone by multiplying both sides by 2: 2A = bh, then divide by h to get 2A/h. Dividing by h alone, giving A/h, keeps the half in.

gold.hint: Multiply both sides by 4, then add 3.

misconceptions.message: Multiplying by 4 gives x − 3 = 4y, then add 3 to both sides: x = 4y + 3. Subtracting 3 instead gives 4y − 3, which is wrong.
Once x − 3 = 4y, add 3 to isolate x: x = 4y + 3. Leaving it as 4(y + 3) never cleared the bracket correctly.

bronze.hint: Multiply the 2 by 3 first, then add the 5.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = 3, so the expression is 2 × 3 + 5. BIDMAS says do the multiply before the add.

guided_steps.hint: Add on the 5 you set aside.

guided_steps.pre: Check by reading the original back: two 3s make 6, plus 5 gives
guided_steps.done: 11 it is. Multiply first, then add.
guided_steps.hint: Same total, counted the other way.

misconceptions.message: Multiplication comes before addition. Do 2 × 3 = 6 first, then add 5 to get 11. Adding first, 2 × (3 + 5) = 16, breaks BIDMAS.

bronze.hint: Multiply 4 by 6 first, then take away 1.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = 6, so 4x means 4 × 6. BIDMAS: multiply before you take away the 1.

misconceptions.message: Multiply before you subtract. Do 4 × 6 = 24 first, then take 1 to get 23. Subtracting first, 4 × (6 − 1) = 20, breaks BIDMAS.

bronze.hint: Work out 3 times 4 and 2 times 5, then add the two results.
bronze.display: Find the value of \(3a + 2b\) when \(a = 4\) and \(b = 5\)

guided_steps.say: Substitute a = 4 and b = 5, giving 3 × 4 + 2 × 5. Do both multiplications first, then add.

guided_steps.done: 22. Multiply each term, then total them.

misconceptions.message: Each term is a multiplication: 3 × 4 = 12 and 2 × 5 = 10, giving 22. Adding coefficient to letter, (3 + 4) + (2 + 5) = 14, is not how substitution works.

bronze.hint: Multiply 5 by negative 2 first, then subtract 3.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = −2, in brackets to keep the sign safe: 5 × (−2) − 3. BIDMAS: multiply first.

guided_steps.hint: A positive times a negative is negative.

guided_steps.pre: Read the original back: five lots of −2 is −10, less 3 is
guided_steps.done: −13. The sign on the product carried through.

misconceptions.message: Multiply first: 5 × (−2) = −10, then subtract 3 to get −13. Subtracting first, 5 × (−2 − 3) = 5 × (−5) = −25, breaks BIDMAS.
A positive times a negative is negative: 5 × (−2) = −10, not 10. Dropping the sign gives 10 − 3 = 7, which is wrong.

bronze.display: Find the value of \(4a - b\) when \(a = 5\) and \(b = 3\)

guided_steps.say: Substitute a = 5 and b = 3, giving 4 × 5 − 3. The multiply comes before the subtraction.

guided_steps.done: 17. Multiply the 4a first, then subtract b.

misconceptions.message: Only the 4a is a product: 4 × 5 = 20, then subtract b to get 17. Treating it as 4(a − b) = 4 × 2 = 8 groups the wrong terms.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = 10, giving (10 ÷ 2) + 3. The division happens before the +3.

guided_steps.pre: Read it back: half of 10 is 5, plus 3 is

misconceptions.message: Divide first: 10 ÷ 2 = 5, then add 3 to get 8. Adding before dividing, (10 + 3) ÷ 2 = 6.5, breaks BIDMAS.

bronze.hint: Multiply 6 by 3 first, then add negative 4, which means subtract 4.
bronze.display: Find the value of \(6x + y\) when \(x = 3\) and \(y = -4\)

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = 3 and y = −4, giving 6 × 3 + (−4). Multiply the 6 × 3 first.

guided_steps.hint: Adding −4 is the same as taking 4 away.

misconceptions.message: Only 6x is a product: 6 × 3 = 18, then add y to get 14. Treating it as 6(x + y) = 6 × (−1) = −6 groups the wrong terms.
y is −4, so you add a negative, which subtracts: 18 + (−4) = 14. Ignoring the minus and doing 18 + 4 = 22 is the slip.

bronze.hint: Multiply 3 by 5 first, then subtract that from 10.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = 5, giving 10 − 3 × 5. The 3 × 5 multiply comes before the subtraction.

guided_steps.pre: Read the original back: 10 take away three 5s (15) is

misconceptions.message: Multiply first: 3 × 5 = 15, then 10 − 15 = −5. Subtracting first, (10 − 3) × 5 = 35, breaks BIDMAS.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = 4, giving 4² + 5. BIDMAS: the power comes first.

guided_steps.pre: Read it back: 4 squared is 16, plus 5 is

misconceptions.message: Square first: 4² = 16, then add 5 to get 21. Adding before squaring, (4 + 5)² = 81, breaks BIDMAS.

silver.hint: Square the 6, work out 5 times 6, then subtract.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = 6, giving 6² − 5 × 6. Power first, then the multiply, then subtract.

guided_steps.done: 6. Square, then subtract five lots of x.

misconceptions.message: Both terms use x = 6: 6² = 36 and 5 × 6 = 30, giving 36 − 30 = 6. Doing (x² − 5) × x = (36 − 5) × 6 = 186 groups it wrongly.

silver.hint: Square negative 3 in brackets to get 9, multiply by 2, then add 1.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = −3, in brackets: 2 × (−3)² + 1. BIDMAS: the power first, before the 2 multiplies.

guided_steps.done: 19. Square the bracket first, multiply, then add.

misconceptions.message: Squaring a negative gives a positive: (−3)² = 9, not −9. Using −9 gives 2 × (−9) + 1 = −17, which is wrong.
The power acts on x alone before the 2 multiplies: 2 × (−3)² = 2 × 9 = 18, then +1 = 19. Doing (2 × −3)² + 1 = 37 squares too much.

silver.hint: Multiply a by t first, then add u.

guided_steps.say: Substitute u = 5, a = 4, t = 3 into v = u + at, giving v = 5 + 4 × 3. The at multiply first.

guided_steps.pre: Read it back: u (5) plus at (12) is
guided_steps.done: 17. Work out at, then add u.

misconceptions.message: The at term is a multiplication done first: 4 × 3 = 12, then add u to get 5 + 12 = 17. Adding u + a before multiplying, (5 + 4) × 3 = 27, breaks BIDMAS.

silver.hint: Square the 2 first, then do each multiplication, then combine.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = 2, giving 3 × 2² − 2 × 2 + 4. BIDMAS: the power 2² first, then the multiplies.

guided_steps.hint: Three lots of the squared value.

guided_steps.done: 12. Square first, then each multiply, then combine.

misconceptions.message: The power acts on x alone: 3 × 2² = 3 × 4 = 12. Squaring the whole 3x, (3 × 2)² = 36, gives 36 − 4 + 4 = 36, which is wrong.

silver.hint: Work out the whole top, 3 squared plus 1, then divide by 5.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = 3, giving (3² + 1) ÷ 5. The whole top is worked out first, then divided by 5.

misconceptions.message: The whole top is divided by 5: (9 + 1) ÷ 5 = 2. Dividing only the 1, giving 9 + (1 ÷ 5) = 9.2, ignores the fraction bar.

silver.hint: Square negative 4 to get 16, work out 2 times negative 4, then subtract 8.

guided_steps.say: Substitute x = −4, in brackets: (−4)² + 2 × (−4) − 8. BIDMAS: the power first.

guided_steps.done: 0. Square first, then the 2x term, then subtract 8.

misconceptions.message: Squaring a negative gives a positive: (−4)² = 16, not −16. Using −16 gives −16 − 8 − 8 = −32, which is wrong.
